tasks.description:
Build the one message row as seven composable parts in `apps/client/src/layers/features/conversation/ui/message/`. `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/ui/message/MessageItem.tsx` (component at :96, 228 lines) and `apps/client/src/layers/widgets/room-view/ui/RoomEntryRow.tsx` (component at :157, 400 lines) plus its four part files (`RoomEntryHeader.tsx` 171, `RoomEntryBody.tsx` 166, `RoomEntryAttachments.tsx` 137, `RoomEntryActions.tsx` 149) are the two parents. Read all six before writing.

## Files to create

`MessageRoot.tsx`, `MessageGutter.tsx`, `MessageAuthor.tsx`, `MessageBody.tsx`, `MessageAttachments.tsx`, `MessageReactions.tsx`, `MessageActions.tsx` — exported from the slice barrel as:

```ts
export const Message = {
  Root: MessageRoot,
  Gutter: MessageGutter,
  Author: MessageAuthor,
  Body: MessageBody,
  Attachments: MessageAttachments,
  Reactions: MessageReactions,
  Actions: MessageActions,
};
```

The composition a host writes:

```tsx
<Message.Root role="assistant" position="first" id={row.id}>
  <Message.Gutter /> {/* avatar rail or corner avatar+timestamp */}
  <Message.Author /> {/* name + timestamp; hidden when position ≠ first */}
  <Message.Body>{renderBody(row.payload)}</Message.Body>
  <Message.Attachments items={row.attachments} />
  <Message.Reactions /> {/* renders null unless capabilities.reactions */}
  <Message.Actions /> {/* one hover-action system */}
</Message.Root>
```

## Invariants — these are the point of the task

- **No `if (surface === 'room')` and no `surface === 'session'` anywhere under `Conversation.Root`.** Behaviour branches on `useConversation().capabilities` only. Task 1.6 adds a source scan that fails on any hit in `features/conversation/ui/` outside `ConversationRoot.tsx`.
- `Message.Root` computes `messageItem({ role, position, density, anchor })` **once** and provides the slot classNames through `message-styles-context.tsx`. No part re-computes the variant.
- `anchor: corner | rail` carries the whole visual difference between the session's corner avatar and the room's avatar rail. `Message.Gutter` reads `anchor` from context; it does not read `surface`.
- `Message.Reactions` renders `null` when `capabilities.reactions` is false.
- `Message.Body` renders a tool card only when `capabilities.toolCards`.
- Every part takes `asChild` (the repo has 188 uses; `Message.Root` and `Message.Author` are the single-element parts that must) and stamps `data-slot` named for the part (`data-slot="message-gutter"`, `"message-author"`, `"message-body"`, …) — 728 uses in the repo and mandated by `contributing/design-system.md`.
- TSDoc on every export.

## Acceptance

- `pnpm --filter @dorkos/client typecheck` and `lint` pass.
- A throwaway render of all seven parts under a `Conversation.Root` with `ROOM_CAPABILITIES` and with `SESSION_CAPABILITIES` produces the two looks. The permanent assertions land in task 1.6 (`Message.test.tsx`) and task 1.7 (the playground matrix); do not leave a scratch file behind.
- `grep -rn "surface ===" apps/client/src/layers/features/conversation/ui/` returns nothing.

```ts
  mentions: false,
```

`apps/client/src/layers/widgets/room-view/model/room-capabilities.ts`:

```ts
export const ROOM_CAPABILITIES: ConversationCapabilities = {
  reactions: true,
  threads: true,
  runWith: false,
  attachments: true,
  toolCards: false,
  mentions: true,
  presence: true,
  turnStatus: false,
  asks: true,
};
/** A DM is a room whose kind changes naming only, so it shares the room's capabilities. */
export const DM_CAPABILITIES = ROOM_CAPABILITIES;
```

That table is the whole of "what is different between the surfaces". Nothing else in the tree may encode it.

## The body renderers

Two implementations, each owned by its host widget, both new files:

- `apps/client/src/layers/widgets/session/ui/render-session-body.tsx` — renders `MessagePartSchema` parts (`packages/shared/src/schemas.ts:2370`) through the existing `features/chat` components: `AssistantMessageContent`, `UserMessageContent`, `StreamingText`, `ThinkingBlock`, `ToolCallCard`, `SubagentBlock`, `MemoryRecallBlock`, `McpSigninCard`, `ErrorMessageBlock`, `CompactBoundaryRow`, `OutputRenderer`, and the three inline prompts (which move to `features/ask` in P3 — leave the current imports alone here).

```ts
/** Turns one message row's opaque payload into its rendered body. */
export type ConversationBodyRenderer = (payload: unknown, ctx: BodyRenderContext) => ReactNode;

export interface BodyRenderContext {
  /** The row this body belongs to. */
  rowId: string;
  /** True while this row is the streaming tail. */
```

Neither renderer knows about the other, and `features/conversation` imports neither.

- `covers:` items name commits by exact subject line (quoted, because a subject contains `: ` which YAML would read as a key) or by SHA. The `post-commit` hook usually writes this for you; curate the prose, leave the frontmatter alone.

P1 is a refactor: one row implementation instead of two, with no visual change. Judge it by the `writing-changelogs` audience test — does someone **operating** DorkOS notice? tasks.subject: [unified-conversation] [P2] Build Conversation.LiveLane with its fixed height and one live region
tasks.description:
`apps/client/src/layers/features/conversation/ui/LiveLane.tsx` — one reserved, fixed-height line, mounted by the host as a **flex sibling of the scroller**, directly above `Conversation.Composer`. Never inside the scrolling element: `apps/client/src/layers/widgets/room-view/ui/RoomSurface.tsx:36-46` documents why in full — a height change inside the scroller moves `scrollHeight` under `useStickToBottom`, which un-pins a reader who never scrolled.

## Geometry — the guarantee is that the number is constant

| Property   | Value                                                                            | Why                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Height     | **fixed `h-6` (24 px), never `min-h`**                                           | 24 px is the smallest step on the spacing scale that gives a 12 px line a 4 px optical gutter either side; the mockup's ~22 px is not on the scale                                                |
| Typography | `text-xs` (12/16), `text-secondary`, agent names `text-primary font-medium`      | matches `ChatStatusStrip` and `RoomPresenceLine` today                                                                                                                                            |
| Padding    | `px-3`, matching the composer's own inset                                        | the lane reads as the composer's shoulder, not a band                                                                                                                                             |
| Overflow   | `flex items-center gap-2 overflow-hidden`, the text node `truncate`              | **it never wraps**; the peek carries what is cut                                                                                                                                                  |
| Empty      | an empty div of the same height, `aria-hidden="true"`, no border, no placeholder | a quiet room looks quiet                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Mobile     | identical height and rules                                                       | a lane that grew on a phone would break the one property it exists for                                                                                                                            |

Mounted **once per conversation surface**. `RoomThreadPanel.tsx` composes its own `Conversation.Root` and therefore its own lane, scoped to the thread.

## Motion budget — nothing new is invented

- Lane content changes: `AnimatePresence mode="wait"` crossfade, **150–200 ms**, keyed on the state's discriminant **plus its label** (`verbKey`'s existing trick, so it animates on a real change and stays still otherwise).
- Working dot: the shipped `STATUS_DOT_PULSE` (`shared/ui/status-dot.ts`), `motion-safe:animate-pulse`. Nothing else in the lane moves.
- Reply hand-off: lane content fades **160 ms** while the reply rises.
- Reduced motion: `useReducedMotion()` and branch **off**, not shorter. The end states all read statically.

## Accessibility — these are hard requirements

- The lane is `role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` **on its text node only**, replacing `RoomPresenceLine`'s announcer (:103-107) one for one — same politeness, same atomicity, and the same `data-testid` split by scope (`room-presence-announcer` / `thread-presence-announcer`) so the shipped browser tests keep their handles.
- **Asks are announced by the existing approval announcer**, not by the lane (`useApprovalAnnouncer`, region at `MessageList.tsx:522-527`). Two live regions both announcing an Ask is the siren the sidebar's contract forbids.
- **Counts, not verbs.** The lane announces the sentence it shows and nothing more; it never announces elapsed ticks.
- **One tab stop.** Enter or Space opens the peek (or the Ask card); Escape closes and returns focus to the lane. When `empty` it is `tabIndex={-1}` and `aria-hidden` and out of the tab order.
- Focus-visible parity: the hover tint step has an explicit `focus-visible:` twin.
- Colour is never the sole indicator: the amber Ask state carries the word **Answer**; the working dot is paired with the sentence.

## Performance

The elapsed tick re-renders the lane once a second while a turn runs, as `ChatStatusStrip` does today. It is a leaf: the tick lives **inside the lane's text node**, not in `Conversation.Root`, so the timeline never re-renders for it.

## Copy — new strings only

`{agent} needs your OK to {verb} {target}` · `Answer` · `1 queued` / `{n} queued`. Everything else is existing copy, verbatim.

## Acceptance

```
pnpm --filter @dorkos/client typecheck && pnpm --filter @dorkos/client lint
```

Lane rendering is asserted for **content**, never for height — jsdom reports every element as 0 × 0, and a unit test that implied otherwise would be one of the vacuous shapes `.claude/rules/testing.md` catalogues. The height claim is the browser test in task 2.6.

tasks.description:
The one server change in P2. "Open its session" in the peek needs the room-author → session mapping, which `GET /api/rooms/:id` does **not** carry (verified: `RoomWithRoster` has no `sessionId` on the room, the member, or the roster entry), and which `specs/room-presence` §15 deliberately kept off the presence signal — _"the in-flight version waits for a design that checks the caller's right to it."_ This is that design.

## The route

```
GET /api/rooms/:id/sessions
→ 200 { bindings: { authorId: string; sessionId: string }[] }
```

- Registered in `apps/server/src/routes/rooms.ts`, beside `GET /:id` (:138).
- Resolve the caller with `resolveCaller(res)`, then `requireVisibleRoom(roomId, caller.id)` — so a room the caller cannot see answers **404**, exactly as `getRoom` does — and then `requirePersonAuthor(caller.id, "see where a room's work runs")`, so an agent cannot enumerate other agents' sessions.
- Body from `RoomSessionLedger.list()` (`apps/server/src/services/rooms/room-session-ledger.ts:97`) filtered to the room. **Ids only**: no session content, no cwd, no status. That is the minimum that makes a link, and the security claim of the route.
- Add the response schema with `.openapi(...)` alongside the other room schemas so `pnpm docs:export-api` picks it up. Regenerating `docs/api/openapi.json` may be left to P5's docs task; if you regenerate here, do it in the same commit as the route.

```ts
 * Every prompt anywhere in the fleet that is waiting on a person.
 *
 * Seeded on mount from `transport.listPendingInteractions()` and then kept live
 * by the global stream, so a window that opened after an Ask was raised shows it
 * as fast as one that was watching.

export function usePendingInteractions(): {
  interactions: readonly InteractionPendingEvent[];
  isLoading: boolean;
};
```

Live updates are two `useEventSubscription` calls writing through `queryClient.setQueryData` — the pattern `use-tunnel-sync.ts` establishes and `contributing/state-management.md` documents:

- `interaction_pending` → **upsert by `interaction.id`**.
- `interaction_resolved` → remove by `interactionId`, and hand the outcome to the receipt store so the card can morph rather than vanish.

`apps/client/src/layers/entities/session/model/session-stream-store.ts:88` holds `pendingInteractions` for the one attached session, fed by the seq'd per-session stream (reducer :802-810, :820-825). Both hold the same `id` (the projector's).

For an id present in both, `remainingMs` comes from the per-session DTO (it is seq'd and fresher) and `roomId` from the global one.

## Headline copy — `lib/ask-headline.ts`, one function, unit-tested

| Kind        | Line                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| approval    | `{agent} wants to {verb} {target}` — verb and target from `displayName` / `title` / `blockedPath`, falling back to `{agent} needs your OK to run {toolName}` when the prompt gives neither |
| question    | `{agent} has a question`                                                                                                                                                                   |
| elicitation | `{agent} needs something from {serverName}`                                                                                                                                                |

The card **never invents** a diff stat or a preview the prompt did not supply. The SDK prompt gives `title`, `displayName`, `description` and `blockedPath`; a diff stat is not among them. "Allow & don't ask again ▾" keeps its **slot** in the action row and is **not built** — it is scope options, tier C. The card ships with **Allow · Deny · Open session**.

## Countdown

From `startedAt + timeoutMs` inside the DTO, ticked locally at 1 s; `formatTimeLeft` reused. Thresholds from `research/20260316_tool_approval_timeout_visibility_ux.md`: neutral above 2 min, **warn at 2 min**, **urgent at 60 s**. The bar is a linear `<progress>`-shaped div with `aria-hidden`; the accessible countdown is the **text**.

## Keyboard and focus

- `A` allows and `D` denies **only when the card has focus** — never a document-level hotkey, because an Ask that lands while you are typing must not swallow a keystroke. Additive to `ToolApproval.tsx:505`'s existing in-card key handling.
- `⌘⇧A` (`useAskShortcut`) moves focus to the next unanswered Ask, opening whatever surface holds it.
- An arriving Ask **never steals focus**. It arrives with the message-entrance grammar (fade + 8 px, spring `stiffness: 320, damping: 28`) and announces itself once through the existing `useApprovalAnnouncer` live region — the card does not add a second announcer.

## Bursts

Two or more pending Asks with the same `sessionId` **and** `interaction.type === 'approval'` **and** the same `toolName` collapse into one `AskStack`: _"Meeting Notes wants to read 5 files ▾"_, expandable to the list, with **Allow all** → `transport.batchApprove(sessionId, toolCallIds)` and **Deny all** → `batchDeny`. **Different agents never stack.**

## Receipts — never a disappearance

On `interaction_resolved` the card morphs in place using the shipped exit transition (`RESOLVE_HOLD_S = 0.4`, `MELT_S = 0.2`, `approval-exit-transition.ts:10,13,37`):

| Outcome                                                       | Line                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| answered by this window                                       | `You allowed this` / `You said no`           |
| answered elsewhere, `resolvedBy` known                        | `Already allowed by {resolvedBy} at {hh:mm}` |
| answered elsewhere, no name                                   | `Already answered at {hh:mm}`                |
| `cancelled` (session gone, agent restarted, turn interrupted) | `No longer needed`                           |
| `expired`                                                     | `Nobody answered in time`                    |

"Never a button that does nothing" is implemented as: the actions are removed **in the same frame** the receipt text appears, and a click that races the resolution is answered by the server's own idempotent no-op (`services/runtimes/claude-code/sessions/session-store.ts:461` returns `false` for an unknown id) and shows the receipt.

## Optimism

Answering writes the receipt immediately and removes the entry from the query cache, then waits for `interaction_resolved` to confirm. A rejected mutation restores the card and surfaces the refusal copy (`features/approvals/lib/decision-refusal.ts`) — including the **403** from the answer guard, which reads as one sentence about needing to be signed in on this machine.

## `features/approvals` re-based

`ApprovalCard` (288) keeps its own data and hooks; **its markup becomes `AskCard.*`**. `format-time-left.ts` and `approval-exit-transition.ts` move to `features/ask` and `features/approvals` imports them from there.
